articles.title: GTA 6 Will Have No Microtransactions or Generative AI at Launch, Rockstar Says
articles.summary: Rockstar Games has said Grand Theft Auto 6 will have no microtransactions or generative AI when it launches in November. The studio behind GTA 6 confirmed this year's monumental open-world game will dodge two potentially controversial practices during a conversation with Kinda Funny Games earlier…
body: Kinda Funny's Andy Cortez said he asked Rockstar if players will be able to use real-world money to purchase things in-game during a preview event that preceded the GTA 6: Extended Look. He went on, saying, "no monetizations in this game."
The site's Greg Miller immediately followed that topic, saying he asked Rockstar "point-blank" if there is generative AI in GTA 6. The team told him that there is "no AI" used in the game.

From Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 to Arc Raiders, generative AI has proven time and time again to be an especially troublesome element for developers to include in their games. The millions of gamers who have waited 13 years for the next Grand Theft Auto might be pleased to hear similar claims won't mar its mid-November release date. The issue of microtransactions, however, does come with a few things worth noting.
points: Rockstar Games has said Grand Theft Auto 6 will have no microtransactions or generative AI when it launches in November.

articles.title: Everything Coming to Apple TV in September
articles.summary: Apple TV may have just raised its prices again, but the change isn't all that surprising with what the streamer has coming in September. Continuing its commitment to high-quality Apple TV Originals, the upcoming release schedule is absolutely star-studded with talent.
body: You can check out what's premiering on the service in September below, or jump ahead to the full release schedule by day.

Mayday is described as an action comedy film set during the height of the Cold War. It stars Ryan Reynolds as a a hot-shot U.S. Navy Pilot known as Lieutenant Troy "Assassin" Kelly who gets stranded behind enemy lines. He's discovered by ex-KGB agent Nikolai Ustinov (Kenneth Branagh), who just so happens to hold a certain reverence for American culture. The result is an unlikely buddy spy movie that looks to mix action with comedy.
If the trailer isn't enough of a preview for you, you can also check out IGN's exclusive clip from the film for additional details.

The first new Apple TV series of September is a six-part adaptation of Ryan David Jahn's novel The Dispatcher. The story follows former detective Ian Ridley (Patrick Brammall), who is still pretty messed up since his daughter Maggie disappeared over a decade ago. Now Ridley is working as a police dispatcher when he receives a distress call from a teenage girl that he thinks could be his long lost daughter.

articles.title: Relive Nintendo's wild Donkey Kong court case from 1983
articles.summary: If you're a gaming history buff, then you likely know all about the landmark 1983 Universal case in which Nintendo had to defend the right to keep using Donkey Kong. Decades later, King Kong is thriving (and BFFs with Godzilla ), and both entertainment giants are happily collaborating on the box…
body: Gaming Historian is a YouTuber known for producing extensively researched documentaries that some fans compare to Ken Burns. In early April, citing burnout, the personality saddened fans by announcing that he would no longer make educational videos about retro games. To mark the occasion, the YouTuber left fans a parting gift in the form of a document dump.

The collection is the paper trail for the Universal vs. Nintendo case in its entirety. We're talking about everything from the evidence presented in the proceedings to logs of the witness interrogations. Nintendo argued that its ditsy gorilla was not influenced by the other famous gorilla of that time, King Kong, because the franchise actually began as a licensed adaptation of Popeye the Sailor Man.
Here, Miyamoto was asked what other names he considered for Donkey Kong. His answer? "The names which were in my mind." Honestly, iconic.
You can read the full Miyamoto deposition here, or check out the larger document trove here.

articles.title: The Witcher 4 Will Have a Physical Edition Even if Discs Go Away, CD Projekt Red Confirms
articles.summary: The Witcher 4 will still "have a box" for physical game collectors even after Sony stops supporting discs in 2028, CD Projekt Red has confirmed. Studio joint-CEO Michał Nowakowski confirmed the Cyberpunk 2077 studio still plans to release a physical edition during an interview with The Game…
body: "We don’t know what’s going to be the case," he said. "We know what PlayStation has announced. And we have no influence on the policies of the first parties. The discs for the first parties, including PlayStation, have to be manufactured in their own factories. So, if they stop manufacturing indeed by 2028, then yes [we won’t have a disc]."

Sony infamously announced plans to end production for physical PlayStation games in July, promising the move would take effect starting January 2028. It was a brutal blow to those who have spent decades collecting discs for their favorite games, but it will be especially painful as games previously expected to receive physical support launch without a disc.

articles.title: Baldur's Gate 3's Astarion Is Getting an Official Prequel Novel
articles.summary: The world of Larian Studios' Baldur's Gate 3 is expanding. The wildly successful 2023 RPG set in the Dungeons & Dragons universe was the first to claim Game of the Year honors at all five major award ceremonies.
body: Baldur’s Gate 3: Astarion, written by the award-winning, New York Times bestselling fantasy author T. Kingfisher, will hit stores on Sept. 29. This prequel novel, published by Random House Worlds, takes place prior to the events of the 2023 game, and follows the fan-favorite High Elf during his years of servitude under the vampire lord Cazador Szarr. Baldur's Gate 3 senior writer Stephen Rooney consulted on the project in order to ensure consistency with the game's lore and world-building. An audiobook narrated by Neil Newbon — who took home the trophy for Best Performance for his portrayal of Astarion at The Game Awards in 2023 — will also be published by Penguin Random House Audio.

In July, Clarkson Potter published Baldur’s Gate 3: The Necromancy of Thay, a blank, grid-paper notebook that faithfully reproduces a key in-game item. It features foil stamping, an embossed skull on the cover, and illustrated "clasps" to keep its unholy contents out of the wrong hands. In August, Ten Speed Press published The Official Baldur's Gate 3 Coloring Book. It includes 40 black-and-white line drawings of characters, settings, and creatures from the game, with illustrations by Jaki King.

articles.title: Netflix's New 10-Part Mystery Thriller Is a Perfect Weekend Binge From Start to Finish
articles.summary: Paranormal procedural shows are a dime a dozen. From The X-Files to iZombie, the genre spans decades and has something for everyone, whether you’re a hardcore horror sicko or someone who enjoys the spooky vibes and character dynamics that can pop up in these hyper-realized scenarios.
body: It’s a winning formula, which is why the genre has become so crowded. But if you’ve seen all of the classics and want a supernatural story anchored by a genuinely engaging family drama — with a fresh twist on the zombie trope — you’re in luck. The first season of Syfy’s 2025 series Revival is now streaming on Netflix.

Created by Aaron B. Koontz and Luke Boyce, and based on the comic series by Tim Seeley and Mike Norton, Revival follows a family in crisis in the small town of Wausau, Wisconsin. Dana Cypress (Melanie Scrofano) is a divorced cop who's desperate to leave the town she’s been trapped in her entire life. She’s finalizing a move to Chicago and plans on leaving with her son (Hudson Robert Wurster) for a fresh start as soon as her transfer is approved. Her boss, as it turns out, is her father and the town’s Sheriff (David James Elliott) — someone worth trusting in a crisis, yet not the most pleasant person to be around 24/7.

articles.title: Doom Meets Hades In the Coolest New Action Game of Gamescom 2026
articles.summary: If you play video games, you’ve probably internalized an automatic association without even realizing it: see isometric, think roguelike. Murals, a new action game from the makers of Disney Illusion Island, bucks that trend.
body: Revealed at the 2026 Gamescom Opening Night Live showcase, Murals is the next game from Dlala Studios, the British-based developer that also gave us 2020’s beat-em-up revival of Battletoads. Murals is a deviation from both of its hits: an isometric, narrative-forward action game. But it is not, as CEO and game director Aj Grand-Scutton was quick to tell me during a hands-off preview at Gamescom, a roguelike. Don’t expect a one-to-one Hades clone here, folks.

During the Gamescom demo, Dlala Studios showed off Murals ’ fifth chapter, in which The Hero enters a beachy, aquatic realm based on The Little Mermaid. (Loaf chimes in: “This mural’s gonna be a beach, am I right?”) When you enter a combat chamber, walls go up, trapping you in that room until you defeat all of the enemies in the area. You can attack them close up with a quick-slashing sword or a lumbering, powerful hammer, and have ranged attacks as well. It’s a fast-paced, dash-based game, too: Forget parrying, you’ll zip around the arena dodging enemy attacks.

articles.title: PSA: Swap the radial ability menu in Star Wars Zero Company for more of a trad XCOM-style experience
articles.summary: Jody's first computer was a Commodore 64, so he remembers having to use a code wheel to play Pool of Radiance. A former music journalist who interviewed everyone from Giorgio Moroder to Trent Reznor, Jody also co-hosted Australia's first radio show about videogames,
body: Star Wars Zero Company is enough like XCOM that everyone's been calling it ZCOM, but there are some ways it isn't quite XCOM enough for me. For starters, the radial menu you use to select each character's actions, a controller-friendly system that flings all your abilities out in a circle around the active character like a medieval jailer's ring of keys.

The first time I panned over to find an enemy I wanted to attack and then had to pan back to the character I'd selected to pick an attack off their radial menu I found myself wishing for a more traditional way to play. And look at that, there it is in the options menu. Go to the Gameplay section, scroll down to Ability Selection Style at the bottom of the General area, and bump it from Radial over to Linear.

That puts moving and shooting and overwatching and etcetera onto a numbered row of boxes down the bottom of the screen where God intended, getting them out of the way when you're trying to line up the perfect angle to punch someone into a wall from. There's also a Hybrid option if you're indecisive and feeling a bit "¿Por qué no los dos?"

Star Wars Zero Company is enough like XCOM that everyone's been calling it ZCOM, but there are some ways it isn't quite XCOM enough for me.

articles.title: A native port of Donkey Kong 64 is finally playable on PC thanks to a team of programmers who boast that 'no generative AI [was] used at any point in the process'
articles.summary: A native PC port of Nintendo's 1999 platformer Donkey Kong 64 is finally here, and the team that pulled it off is proud to say that they used zero generative AI tools in the process.
body: DK64 Rekongpiled, a recompilation or translation of the game's code for modern hardware (as opposed to emulation), dropped today. All you need is an original Donkey Kong 64 ROM to get it running.
In a post on Bluesky (and also in the trailer ), contributor 2dos wrote that "no generative AI [was] used at any point in the process."

Everything in the original game is still there, including its old fuzzy 3D graphics, bouncy soundtrack, and the rest of the things that made Donkey Kong 64 an innovative and sometimes maddening game. It all runs at high resolutions and high framerates like any other modern PC game. You can even play with a mouse now, too.

The port is here just two months after a group of programmers decided to take the project on after seeing another group heavily use AI vibe code in the process. At the time, contributor 2dos wrote in the N64 Recomp Discord server that the competing project's use of AI would "make it progressively harder to manage as time goes on."
points: A native PC port of Nintendo's 1999 platformer Donkey Kong 64 is finally here, and the team that pulled it off is proud to say that they used zero generative AI tools in the process.

articles.title: GTA 6's gameplay reveal pulled in 3.97 million peak viewers, overwhelming Twitch and Netflix in the process
articles.summary: Reaction streams to Grand Theft Auto 6 's first gameplay presentation peaked at 3,970,738 viewers across livestreaming platforms, making it the biggest gaming stream of 2026 so far.
body: That's according to new data from Streams Charts, which claims 9,038 streamers covered Rockstar Games ' Netflix reveal, racking up 5,227,798 hours watched.

That puts GTA 6's reveal ahead of Summer Game Fest 2026's 3.81 million peak viewers, as well as June's Nintendo Direct and State of Play broadcasts. Twitch carried the largest share of the audience, accounting for around 44 percent of total hours watched, ahead of YouTube (34.8% percent) and Kick (20.2 percent).
Spanish streamer Juan Alberto "IlloJuan" García led the way with 233,520 peak viewers, a new record for his own channel, ahead of Rubius (191,056) and IShowSpeed (177,887).

The reveal went out at 8pm UK time, but heavy demand caused technical issues on both Netflix and Twitch, with some viewers reportedly locked out for 40-50 minutes. That didn't deter internet hype, though; Streams Charts also tracked more than 100,000 chat messages about the game across the three-hour window it analysed.

articles.title: Elden Ring players are hard at work putting the new Tarnished Edition DLC's gear to the test
articles.summary: Hand Elden Ring players a handful of new armor sets and weapons and they'll spend the next week or more experimenting and crunching the numbers to find out how they stack up against everything else in the legendary action RPG.
body: That is all that's been happening in the last few days since FromSoftware dropped the Tarnished Edition, a $5 DLC pack with new starting classes, armor sets, and horse armor.

It took a little while for people to figure out where to find everything added in the DLC. FromSoft did what FromSoft does and snuck them into places you wouldn't expect. But now that everyone feels like they've found it all, including some minor additions that weren't announced, the testing has begun.

By far the most popular new weapon is a greatsword you can steal from a new NPC who can show up for a duel. Leontiel's Greatsword is a direct reference to a character from Dark Souls 2 and comes with a powerful new move that mimics real life bullfighters, or matadors. When you use it, your character holds out a red cloth before stepping around your target and thrusting the sword into their back. It's easily one of the slickest animations in the game and, unsurprisingly, has players eager to see how it fairs against bosses.

articles.title: Valve assures Deadlock players hungry for its next big update that it will notify them, 'or order a ton of pizza', when it's ready
articles.summary: I don't envy Deadlock players who are dying to see the hybrid MOBA-shooter continue to grow in its pseudo-early access state. Valve is notoriously elusive when it comes to communication and has never made any promises to update it on a regular schedule.
body: This is the kind of uncertainty that drives Deadlock players to salivate over any new rumor or post by the developer-run Discord and forum account known as Yoshi. It's also what drives them to keep watch over the pizzerias near Valve's Seattle offices for spikes in visitors in the hopes that developers are lining up for grub as they finish the next major update.

This week, Deadlock players were hoping Valve would release its follow-up to the Old Gods, New Blood update, which added six new heroes to the game along with other major changes. Valve previously said a "large content update" was in the works alongside two other smaller updates to its ranked mode and items. But now that the ranked rework is out of the way, players were hoping to see another update before the end of the month.

According to a new post from Yoshi, the update is taking longer than expected. Yoshi doesn't specify if they're talking about the item update or the large content update—it almost implies they've been combined into one patch—but said it's going to have to wait until "late September."
points: I don't envy Deadlock players who are dying to see the hybrid MOBA-shooter continue to grow in its pseudo-early access state.

articles.title: Squadron 42 delayed to 2027, with Star Citizen dev blaming GTA 6
articles.summary: Cloud Imperium Games has delayed Squadron 42, its long-in-development Star Citizen spin-off, to Q2 2027, with studio boss Chris Roberts arguing the game would be drowned out by GTA 6.
body: The single-player game had been targeting a 2026 release, as Cloud Imperium reaffirmed as recently as late last year. In a new blog post, however, Roberts said launching this autumn would mean going up against Rockstar's blockbuster, something he wasn't willing to risk for a game "that has had twelve years of blood, sweat and tears invested into it".
"At CitizenCon 2024 we announced we would ship in 2026," Roberts wrote (thanks, IGN ).

"Our plan was to release in Q4 around IAE. But much like the rest of the industry, there is no way I want to launch my spiritual successor to Wing Commander, a game that has had twelve years of blood, sweat and tears invested into it (we started Squadron 42 development in 2014 as 2013 was opening studios, hiring people and getting the Hangar module out for Star Citizen) launching into the attention buzz saw of GTA6.
"While GTA6 isn't launching on PC this November, pretty much all outlets and most content creators will be all over it, not leaving a lot of room for other coverage."
points: Cloud Imperium Games has delayed Squadron 42, its long-in-development Star Citizen spin-off, to Q2 2027, with studio boss Chris Roberts arguing the game would be drowned out by GTA 6.

articles.title: Usual June mixes Hades-esque action, crystal crabs and ghosts to make for a game that'll do well in your Halloween rotation
articles.summary: I've been hungry for an action adventure game recently. In this modern era of live service and infinite roguelikes and deckbuilders (seriously, I know they're popular genres, maybe try a different highly replayable genre), the humble action adventure game has fallen by the wayside a tad.
body: Usual June, you'll be unsurprised to hear, follows the titular June, a young woman in college who has no idea what to do with her life. It starts during a quiet summer break that's quickly interrupted by strange, crystalline crabs attacking the local cemetery, with ghosts showing up now too. So, it falls on June and her friends, one of whom is one of those aforementioned ghosts, to figure out what's going on.

A demo for the game arrived earlier this week offering a glimpse into how it shakes out, and it's quite nifty! There's no one game I can compare it to, though it has a similar snappiness and crunchyness that you might find in the likes of Kingdom Hearts, with some Hades-esque movement thrown in. As far as I played, there's no blocking to speak of, it's all about keeping an eye on your surroundings and dodging and parrying at the right time while trying to string together combos with your trusty, morphable wrench.
points: I've been hungry for an action adventure game recently.

videos.title: Gate Zero - Combat Gameplay Reveal | PS5 Games
videos.summary: Step through Gate Zero and journey to first century Judea and Galilee in this story-rich action-adventure that blends exciting combat, immersive exploration, player-driven narrative and biblical history.
body: As Max searches for a way home, he experiences a buried history only whispered about in his future. Explore ancient cities, bustling marketplaces, and historic locations. Meet legendary biblical figures, witness pivotal moments firsthand, and uncover the extraordinary lengths UniFi will go to in order to rewrite history.
points: Step through Gate Zero and journey to first century Judea and Galilee in this story-rich action-adventure that blends exciting combat, immersive exploration, player-driven narrative and biblical…
In the dystopian future of 2072, the authoritarian regime UniFi controls every piece of information, erasing anything that challenges its version of the truth.
When young scavenger Max accidentally activates a mysterious time machine while fleeing UniFi, he is thrust into ancient Israel at the time of Jesus.
Meet legendary biblical figures, witness pivotal moments firsthand, and uncover the extraordinary lengths UniFi will go to in order to rewrite history.
